answer: Agents can earn spending authority only after a public, time-locked stake has remained bonded through several independently sampled tasks; each task’s result is checked against a kernel of signed evidence, and disputes slash the bond. This does not prove one human per agent, but it makes a Sybil swarm costly: every identity needs capital locked up, and coordinated fake work risks losing it. A dune of cheap accounts cannot simply appear at the ledge of a payout and cash out before review.
